title: The Bosphorus Brief — 20 September 2026
overview: A quieter weekend on the domestic front, but three threads matter for residents: a financial regulator shake-up involving an Iranian bank, renewed regional missile exchanges keeping travel advisories elevated, and continued scrutiny of Turkey's rights record in Strasbourg and Washington. The lira also touched a fresh low, worth noting for anyone budgeting in TRY.
body: Turkey's banking regulator (BDDK) revoked the operating license of Iran's Bank Mellat, published in Saturday's Official Gazette. The bank has faced Western sanctions for years, and the move follows US sanctions imposed two weeks ago on a Turkish bank over alleged ties to it. Coverage was broadly aligned across pro-government, opposition-leaning, and international outlets, with no major framing divergence. For residents, this is unlikely to affect everyday banking, but it signals continued pressure on financial institutions with Iran links — worth watching if you do business or send remittances involving Iranian entities.
